Package sootup.core.signatures

Class SignatureInterner

java.lang.Object
sootup.core.signatures.SignatureInterner
public final class SignatureInterner extends Object
Hash-conses (interns) the identifier objects of sootup.core.signatures: for a given value there is at most one live instance, so equal signatures are the same object and may be compared with ==.

Interning happens on the constructed object itself, so identity follows each type's own equals/hashCode - there is no separate cache key that could drift out of sync with them. The interners hold their entries weakly, so a signature that nothing references any more is collected as usual.

This class exists in sootup.core because the constructors it calls are package-private: it is the only way to create these types, which is what makes the interning invariant hold. Most callers should not use it directly but go through an IdentifierFactory, which is the language-aware entry point. sootup.core itself has no IdentifierFactory implementation available (that lives in the language modules, which depend on this one), so code inside this module - its tests in particular - uses these methods instead.
